title: Smart Wall Switches and Dimmers: Lights On by Voice, App or Remote
subtitle: A smart wall switch replaces the switch you already have, so a light can be turned on by voice, phone or a small remote.
excerpt: Tired of crossing a dark room to find the switch? A smart wall dimmer can turn on a ceiling light by voice, app or a handheld remote. Here is how they work, what the listings show, and what to check before buying.
author: Nickel And Gadget Editors

sections.content: Many of us know the routine: you come home at dusk with your hands full, and the light switch is on the far side of the room. Or you are settled in bed and the overhead light is still on.

A smart wall switch is one answer. It takes the place of the switch on your wall, so the ceiling light or fixture it controls can also be turned on by speaking to a voice assistant, tapping a phone, or pressing a small handheld remote.
A note on where this comes from: the details below are drawn from three Best Buy product listings and their Q&A sections. They are not tested by us and have not been confirmed by Lutron, the maker.
How a smart switch is different

Smart plugs control lamps that plug into an outlet. Smart bulbs put the brains inside the bulb. A smart switch is different because it replaces the wall hardware itself. That means it works with lights wired into the ceiling or wall. Best Buy's Q&A says one Caseta switch can control multiple bulbs.

The switches in this article are from Lutron's Caseta line. They are dimmers, so you can set a light lower instead of full brightness. The listings say they work with popular voice assistants, including Amazon Alexa, Google Home and Apple Home.

There is one piece many shoppers miss: for phone or voice control, the 3-way kit page says the Lutron Smart Bridge is required. Think of the bridge as a small translator box that passes your commands to the switch. Some listings say it is included, and some do not. The bridge's separate price is not given on the pages we read, so the true total cost for a kit that leaves it out is unknown.

If one light can be turned on from two places, such as the top and bottom of the stairs, that is called a 3-way setup. A regular single switch is not the right fit there. Lutron sells a separate 3-way kit with a Pico remote for those spots.

items: Check for the bridge. Read the box or listing to see whether a Smart Bridge is included. The single dimmer and 3-way pages do not clearly say it is. If it is not included, its price is not listed in the pages we read, so check current price before you buy.
Check your bulbs. The listings say dimmable LED bulbs are needed. The single dimmer is rated for 150W of LED or 600W of incandescent. Look for the word "dimmable" on the bulb package.
Know your wiring. Best Buy's Q&A says the kit and the 3-way kit need no neutral wire. The single dimmer's page does not say, so check the box.
Match the switch to the spot. One switch for one light is simple. Two switches for one light means you want the 3-way kit.
Look at monthly fees. Best Buy's listings show none, though we did not check this against Lutron's own terms.

Plan for installation. This means working with household electrical wiring, and the listings do not say whether it is a do-it-yourself job. If you are not comfortable, a licensed electrician is a sensible choice.
Check the return policy before you open the box.

sections.content: Setting it up and using it well

Installation starts at the breaker box. Turn off the power to that switch before anyone removes the old one. If the light is controlled from two places, you need the 3-way kit. If you are unsure which breaker it is, or the wires do not look like the instructions, stop and call an electrician.
Phone and voice control need the Smart Bridge, so follow the setup steps in the box. After that, you can link the switch to your voice assistant and give the light a simple name like "bedroom light."

The 3-way kit's Pico remote is a small button pad that uses one CR2032 battery, included. The kit's Q&A says a Pico can be mounted with a wall bracket, sold separately. Either way, it can offer a way to control the light with no phone and no talking.

A smart switch is a convenience, not a safety system. It cannot call for help or detect a fall. Voice and app control depend on the Smart Bridge. The lights also need power to answer commands, so do not leave the switch turned off at the wall. In an emergency, call 911.
sections.label: Good to Know

sections.content: If wall wiring sounds like more than you want to take on, smart plugs or smart bulbs need no tools at all. But if a ceiling light is the one you wish you could control from your chair, a smart dimmer is worth a look. Start with one room and see how it fits your routine.
